subject: Animation
title: Mexican Animation and Día de los Muertos
description: A micro-lesson that makes Mexican Animation and Día de los Muertos usable.

hook.text: Mexican visual culture — vibrant colors, mythology, and folk art — has deeply influenced global animation.

buildup.text: Pixar's Coco drew heavily from Mexican traditions around Día de los Muertos and earned massive cultural praise.

discovery.text: Mexican studios are now building their own animated features rather than waiting for Hollywood to tell their stories.

twist.text: Some Mexicans criticized Coco as cultural extraction — a U.S. studio profiting from traditions it did not own.

climax.text: Mexico's animation industry is growing, driven by a desire to tell authentic Mexican stories on a global stage.

punchline.text: Mexico is tired of Hollywood telling its stories and is making its own.

quiz.question: How has Mexican culture influenced global animation?
options: Mexico is the world's largest animation outsourcing market
Its vibrant visual traditions inspired films like Coco, while Mexican studios now create their own features
